title: Battery Ops family workspace
lede: Battery Ops now answers the family-level questions first—what is available, what needs attention, what metadata identifies the pool—and reveals numbered units only when an operator needs to act on them.

stats.n: Measured in the matched 1280×720 captures; the old card continues to the viewport edge
Independent rows remove the dead space created by unequal unit counts

sections.heading: Family operations at a glance
sections.note: Same 1280×720 viewport and the same FX6 / Gold Mount counts, labels, category, and location. The before capture is the currently deployed page; the after capture uses a development-only fixture copied from that operating snapshot so no inventory mutation was required.

pairs.title: From an always-open tile wall to a family workspace
pairs.sub: Look at the first FX6 family and where Gold Mount begins.
pairs.beforeCap: Every unit renders immediately, generic Add and Brother CSV actions compete with the name, and unequal families create a coupled two-column layout.
pairs.afterCap: Availability, status, threshold, labels, QR, and product mix lead; Add units, Export labels, Edit metadata, and Show units name the operator's next move.

changes.h: The live number was easy to misread as an editable field
changes.was: A dense wall of numbered tiles carried the truth but offered no concise explanation of how the count changes.
changes.now: The family says that numbered availability comes from unit status, then routes new physical stock through Add units and count corrections through each unit menu.

changes.was: Battery Ops could add the next numbered range, but could not attach an existing product to those units during receiving.
changes.now: The receiving dialog keeps the exact range, before/after count, and reason while adding an optional active-product assignment.

changes.h: Metadata was hidden behind an unlabeled family link
changes.was: Location and category were present, while threshold, QR identity, label readiness, product mix, and the edit destination were not grouped as an operational summary.
changes.now: The family workspace exposes those fields together and provides an explicit Edit metadata handoff to the existing audited detail flow.

verification: 20 focused tests pass across Battery Ops reads, stale repair, unit adjustments, and the new experience source contract.
TypeScript and focused ESLint pass with no findings in the changed files.
Full app build passes with the final Battery Ops source and development fixture.
Authenticated desktop browser proof covers the collapsed family workspace, unit expansion and status filters, and product-aware receiving dialog without submitting a mutation.

Narrow viewport proof: unavailable because the connected in-app browser does not expose a viewport override; responsive source and the production build pass, but this is not a visual narrow-screen claim.
notes: No schema, migration, custody policy, or production inventory was changed.
The normal Preview database is behind the dirty shared Prisma client, so the review uses an authenticated development-only fixture gated to NODE_ENV=development and the fixture query.
Creating the Football Sony Battery family remains separate operational work under GAP-74.
